        "Parent/root read all 2256 owned full-show lines across 15 actual changed/renamed paths. The observer, outgoing implementation and stream helpers move to protocol_shared; dependencies and EWS imports/trait implementations change too. No test file or new assertion is added. This is a human functional extraction, not a bulk exclusion or proven behavior-preserving move.",
        "ProtocolClient supplies the protocol identifier and shutdown in the historical design. SendCapableClient adds asynchronous send_message with owned mailbox data. The EWS constructor supplies a function that obtains endpoint_url, queries nsIMsgOutgoingServer and creates XpComEwsClient. EWS converts generic Bcc mailboxes back to EWS recipients; null address objects still return NS_ERROR_NULL_POINTER and optional names remain Option values.",
        "The generic server lazily constructs Arc<ClientT>, obtains its key and registers a removal observer before setting OnceCell. Constructor or observer failure leaves the cache unset, so the comment that the constructor is called only once needs a successful-initialization qualification. The observer matches both topic and key, queues shutdown and removes itself; returning from observe is not proof that shutdown completed. The current service notifies with server.key before clearing preferences.",
        "The historical server_type method changes from constant ews to self.client()?.protocol_identifier(), which can create a client during type lookup. Fixed accepted code instead reads mail.smtpserver.<key>.type. Its comment names an authentication/password/type recursion risk. That later fix is accepted comparison context, not a new audit of Bug2067685 or a reproduced initialization failure.",
        "The review adopts endpoint_url for local names while keeping PrefName::EwsUrl mapped to stored ews_url. The existing namespace lesson is reused after matching both the fixed mapping and getter. Source naming and persisted data compatibility are distinct; the optional naming request does not establish a global rename rule.",
        "This extraction removes the native ForgetPassword result conversion added by4911: its new shared function calls the native method and then returns Ok. The fixed accepted shared function again returns to_result. Git blame metadata locates that restoration at later manifest5335/2d38d3fd20d0, without reading or crediting that future patch. Preserve the regression and accepted correction separately; no native failure was injected.",
        "The string parsing helpers become public mailnews_string_glue functions with Safety sections. They scan raw pointers until NUL and then decode lossily; lossy decoding does not validate pointer lifetime, readable range or termination. Current removal observer is one checked consumer. The historical manual-testing claim about XPCOM strings is attributed source commentary, not proof for every raw-string origin.",
        "The manual GetPasswordWithUI entry point preserves the special successful cancellation status directly and maps internal None back to it. Its source comment explains why the normal macro is bypassed. The moved read_stream remains a single Available/Read pass with an explicit limitation that all wanted bytes may not be present; no complete-message or arbitrary-stream guarantee is inferred.",
        "Manual readability review checked state publication, early failure returns, stored keys, optional address names, comments and Rust receiver/ownership contracts. Several retained comments have grammar or overbroad wording; they are not new style rules. No Rust/Cargo build, message send, password UI, stream error, observer lifecycle or native test ran.",

The obsolete status-feedback interface request is adopted. The endpoint-name question is explicitly optional; author replies with endpoint_url, and actual source adopts local naming while preserving stored ews_url.",

The chapter describes folders as the join between message metadata, optional raw local data and protocol/server interaction, with MAY-qualified capabilities rather than a universal operation set.",
